name: scramble
summary: A monospace headline that resolves out of noise: every character is blanked, then rolls 45 times at 15ms while each line starts 200ms behind the one above it.

iterations.description: How many times each character changes before it settles. Upstream's MAX_CELL_ITERATIONS in fx1.

tick.description: Milliseconds between a character's changes. Upstream's fx1 setTimeout interval.

lineDelay.description: Milliseconds each line waits behind the one above it. Upstream's (line.position + 1) * 200.

deviations.what: Only fx1 is ported. fx2 through fx6, the effects map and trigger(effect) are dropped, and with them Cell's color / originalColor fields and the randomNumber helper from utils.js that fx3 and fx6 use.
deviations.why: fx1 is the effect trigger() runs by default and the only one the demo's first button shows. Shipping six variants behind an option would be five untested code paths in a library where each effect is meant to be one thing; the other five are better ports in their own right if they are ever wanted.

deviations.what: Splitting.js is replaced by anime.js' splitText, and the Line/Cell tree is built from split.lines plus each line's [data-char] elements instead of from Splitting's results[0].lines.
deviations.why: Splitting is a second dependency for a job the vendored anime.js already does, and the effect contract limits an effect to vendor keys the manifest lists. The structure the port needs -- characters grouped per line, positions counted from the start of each line -- is the same either way.

deviations.what: The run is triggered by an IntersectionObserver the first time the section is on screen, once per mount, rather than by a button. A resize re-split rebuilds the cells but does not replay.
deviations.why: Upstream is a demo page with six buttons. A section has no button, and a headline that re-scrambles every time the window is dragged is noise rather than an effect.

deviations.what: Every setTimeout id is kept and cleared on destroy, and the split is reverted.
deviations.why: Upstream keeps none, because its page never tears the effect down. Here a destroy mid-run would otherwise leave the headline as the blanked cells the run starts from, and a page transition would keep firing timers into detached nodes.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the text is not split and the run never starts.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest, and the headline is already the finished content.
